arabic: خان؛ نُزل للمسافرين؛ أو هان اسم علم
note: Han is translated according to the supplied Arabic caravanserai/inn sense, with the personal-name alternative retained. Context should determine whether a proper name is intended.
Jean is translated as the regional singular noun for jeans, as specified in Arabic; it can also be a personal name in other contexts.
Amber is translated as ambergris/perfumery fragrance substance according to Arabic, rather than the fossil resin sense of English amber.
Chan is translated as the historical caravanserai/inn sense specified in Arabic, not as a personal name.
Merlin is translated as the small falcon (Dutch smelleken), not the legendary wizard.
Arabic contains قيمة جبل; the mountain-peak sense should be قمة جبل. English and Dutch use peak/summit.
German Tiger is tiger / tijger. Arabic نمر can be ambiguous or refer to leopard in precise zoological usage; ببر is the unambiguous tiger term.
